title: Google Family Link Usage Failure Rate
dataSources: Canvas assignments (`canvas:assignment`), Khan Academy SAT practice (`khan:sat`), Family Link usage (`familylink:usage`), and OurHome chores (`ourhome:chore`).
app: Canvas LMS exports, Khan Academy SAT practice, Google Family Link screen-time data, and OurHome chore tracking streamed to Splunk.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=familylink:usage
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(usage_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by app_name
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often Google Family Link usage records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each app name.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize usage_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per app name.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It reveals which parts of your Google Family Link usage data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
